caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular grid consisting of sixteen squares, each displaying a unique embroidery or needlework pattern. The patterns are rendered on a light background, possibly white or beige, with an open-weave that simulates embroidery canvas. The squares are arranged in four rows and four columns, and each square features a distinct combination of colors and geometric motifs. The color palette includes green, pink, red, blue, brown, beige, and black. At the top left, there is a diagonal green and beige chevron pattern. Adjacent to it, towards the center top, there is a motif resembling a butterfly with wings in pink, beige, and black. To the right, a pattern consists of red and pink rounded shapes with black grid lines and white X marks inside red squares. The other squares display various arrangements including diamond shapes in red, beige, blue, brown, and pink, checkerboard patterns, vertical stripes, and flower-like motifs. The whole grid is bordered on the left side by a vertical strip of patterned lace in a beige tone with floral designs, which extends slightly beyond the rectangle of the patterned squares. The image is signed “Ruth M. Barrow” at the bottom right corner and marked with the code “A 3850 - A” at the bottom left. The background of the entire piece is a plain, light color.
title: Sampler (Stitching)
cluster: #01 — Textile Arts: Quilts, Samplers, and Embroideries
